reviewed_caption:
A motionless spider might just be waiting. In laboratory Portia fimbriata, researchers looked at rest posture, twitching, retinal movements, responses to sound and rebound after a disturbed night. Four of ten spiders tested during REM-like bouts did not react within ten seconds, but reacted when awake. Thirteen paired recordings showed mean REM-like time rising from 9.4 to 16.9 minutes after fly disturbance. Behavioral evidence supports sleep with REM-like periods, not proof of dreaming or direct neural equivalence.

Geiger et al. (2026), PNAS. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2618030123
